title: GPU pocket-budgeting quota model for weights, KV leases, and activation fairness
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We observe intermittent OOMs and long tail latency for mixed-priority inference workloads when continuous batching competes with large persistent weight and KV cache footprints. Existing soft-watermark and headroom heuristics are tuned at the GPU level but do not provide predictable per-tenant or per-request guarantees.

Goal: Design and prototype a 'pocket-budgeting' quota model: a lightweight, request-aware memory budgeting layer that reserves small contiguous 'pockets' of headroom for active requests (activations + transient KV windows) while maintaining global accounting for weights and long-lived KV. The model should dynamically rebalance pockets across tenants and workloads, cooperate with KV lease/TTL policies, and expose signals for graceful preemption and fallback.

Scope: prototype allocator + simulator + telemetry; API signals exposed to scheduler for preemption/fallback; a canary rollout plan for dedicated pools. Not in scope: changes to model storage layout or quantization kernels (those are follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Allocator prototype integrated into the serving runtime with an opt-in flag and documentation
End-to-end simulator demonstrating >40% reduction in OOMs for mixed latency and batchy workloads on 8-GPU cluster traces
KV lease policy (adaptive TTL) implemented in prototype and validated against long-tail KV retention cases
Telemetry surfaces per-pocket occupancy, pocket churn, eviction-rate, and cross-tenant steal events in Console dashboard
Canary on dedicated pool with canary traffic shows no >2x tail-latency regressions and successful graceful fallback to lower-model variants under pressure
tasks: Design pocket accounting data structure and invariants (owner, min_reserve, flexible_cap, lease_id)
Implement allocator hook in runtime (allocation, commit, reclaim, steal) behind feature flag
Build offline simulator that replays recent production traces (tokens/sec, KV size distribution, request priority)
Implement adaptive KV lease TTL heuristic using EWMA of recent reuse intervals
Expose metrics and tracing spans for pocket lifecycle and KV lease decisions
Create canary rollout runbook and rollback criteria for Dedicated pools
Update docs/SDK with opt-in config, tuning knobs, and recommended defaults
approach_and_tradeoffs: Pocket concept: small contiguous headroom slices (e.g., 32–128MB) reduce fragmentation and let the runtime satisfy short-lived activation bursts without touching large weight/KV reservations
Adaptive vs fixed pockets: adaptive pockets improve utilization for bursty workloads but add complexity; prototype will start with fixed-size pockets plus an adaptive top-up policy
KV leases: shortening TTL reduces KV pressure but increases miss rate; our EWMA-based TTL trades off a small increase in KV misses for lower eviction churn under high contention
Preemption strategy: prefer stealing flexible_cap pockets from low-priority tenants before evicting long-lived KV or spilling weights; worst-case fallback is model variant downgrade

Latency/throughput tradeoff: over-reserving pockets increases tail predictability at the cost of raw throughput. The target is to reduce OOMs and tail latency for P0/P1 customers while keeping P3 degradation graceful
simulation_results_summary: Baseline traces (mixed small chat + long embedding batches) produced OOM rate of 0.82% across 1000 node-minutes
Pocket-budgeting prototype with fixed 64MB pockets reduced OOM rate to 0.27% and reduced 95th percentile token latency by 18% in the simulator
Adaptive TTL for KV leases lowered KV churn by 33% with a measured 4% increase in KV miss rate (acceptable for conversational workloads in our tests)
Aggressive pocket-steal policy recovered 70% of headroom within 120ms on simulated burst events without a major impact on victim tenant latency in most scenarios
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Pocket fragmentation over long-running workloads leading to wasted reserved memory -> Mitigation: periodic compaction reclaim job and pocket-coalescing heuristic
Risk: Increased KV miss rate hurting quality for certain customers -> Mitigation: label-sensitive policy (customer opt-out) and gradual TTL ramp with canary monitoring
Risk: Complexity in cross-tenant fairness -> Mitigation: clear tenant priority classes and quota borrowing limits; telemetry to detect unfair steals
Risk: Runtime stability due to new allocator code paths -> Mitigation: feature-flagged rollout, heavy unit + integration tests, and canary on dedicated pools only initially
canary_and_rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal perf cluster experiments with production trace replay (QA only)
Phase 1: opt-in canary on small Dedicated pool (5% of Dedicated capacity) with verbose telemetry and rollback criteria
Phase 2: expand to 25% Dedicated traffic with tuned defaults and SDK config exposed
Phase 3: global rollout to all Dedicated pools and optional Hosted API opt-in after further validation
